column1: # One row per SINGLE run (no medians). lean-align f465a57 against minibwa c07de5c, 4 threads on 4 cores. make_figs.py reads this file for figs/vs_minibwa* and picks up extra rows (new rep numbers, new sizes) without edits.

# experiment gz5m: 5M pairs from gz files, Testing/ec2/run.sh (bench.py), raw rows from Testing/results/ec2_check/{nova5m,hiseq5m}/timing.tsv: wall incl. index load, cpu incl. both gzips. Gbp_hr = Gbp / wall, Gbp_core_hr = Gbp / cpu.

# experiment stream: streamed from the network, no file on disk (NovaSeq HG002 30x 10/20/40M pairs; HiSeq GIAB D1_S1_L001 whole lane 33,916,091 pairs). Values copied from runs.tsv (see its header and README for what cpu_s and the rates mean per source).
# NOT included: the minibwa NovaSeq 10M streamed run (742.8 s) because its wall time includes a 158.9 s cold index load. The lean-align 'before' builds are not in this file.

# experiment stream: NovaSeq, the FIRST 10M pairs (3.020 Gbp), 3 runs per tool, SAME pipeline for both tools (resuming downloader, gunzip, cat > /dev/null sink, index pre-cached, alternating runs), 4 threads. From S-P, branch bench/stream-results (Testing/results/stream/runs/n10000000_{ours,minibwa}_rep{1,2,3}/result.json). wall_s includes the index load; cpu_s = aligner CPU only (gunzip/curl not included).

# experiment stream_single: the older single streamed runs (NovaSeq 10/20/40M with md5 or /dev/null sinks and different downloaders; the HiSeq lane for both tools). make_figs.py plots experiment 'stream' where a data set has rows of it and falls back to stream_single otherwise (today: HiSeq).
